target_audience.primary_persona: Software developers who want to delegate coding tasks to AI agents while maintaining control over their codebase
secondary_personas: Tech leads managing multiple development tasks simultaneously
Solo developers working on complex projects who need productivity multipliers
pain_points: Manual coding is slow and tedious for repetitive or boilerplate tasks
Existing AI coding assistants require constant supervision and context-switching
Merging AI-generated code into main branch is risky without proper isolation
AI assistants forget context between sessions leading to repeated explanations
Validating AI-generated code quality requires manual review effort
goals: Automate implementation of well-defined coding tasks
Run multiple AI coding agents in parallel for faster delivery
Safely integrate AI-generated code with built-in QA and conflict resolution
Build and ship features faster without sacrificing code quality
Maintain persistent context so AI remembers project patterns and decisions
target_audience.usage_context: Desktop application used during active development sessions. Developers create tasks via Kanban board, watch agents work in real-time terminals, and review/merge completed work. Works alongside existing development tools and git workflows.

product_vision.one_liner: Autonomous multi-agent coding framework that plans, builds, and validates software for you
product_vision.problem_statement: AI coding assistants require constant supervision, lack persistent memory, and produce code that's risky to merge without extensive review. Developers need a way to delegate entire coding tasks safely.
product_vision.value_proposition: Turret provides true autonomous coding with isolated git worktrees for safety, built-in QA validation before human review, AI-powered merge conflict resolution, and persistent memory across sessions - letting developers describe what they want and get validated, mergeable code.
success_metrics: Number of tasks completed autonomously without human intervention
Time saved per task compared to manual implementation
Percentage of first-attempt QA passes (code quality)
User retention and daily active usage
Number of parallel agents utilized per session

existing_features: Kanban board for visual task management
Autonomous task execution with Claude AI agents
Parallel execution with up to 12 agent terminals
Isolated git worktree workspaces for safe development
Self-validating QA pipeline before human review
Memory Layer for cross-session context retention (Graphiti)
Insights chat interface for codebase exploration
Linear integration for external task sync
known_gaps: Advanced conflict analysis checks not yet implemented
Merge completion recording not fully implemented
Password hashing needs proper implementation in tests
technical_debt: Some TODO comments indicating incomplete implementations in merge/conflict handling
Test mocking could be improved for password handling
Large node_modules footprint from Electron dependencies

alternatives: GitHub Copilot - AI pair programming assistant
Claude Code CLI - Terminal-based Claude coding
Cody (Sourcegraph) - AI coding assistant with codebase context
differentiators: True autonomous execution - delegates entire tasks, not just autocomplete
Isolated git worktrees - changes never touch main branch until reviewed
Built-in QA validation loop - catches issues before human review
AI-powered merge conflict resolution - handles complex integrations
Persistent Memory Layer - agents remember context across sessions
Parallel multi-agent execution - up to 12 simultaneous tasks
Visual Kanban task management - not just a CLI or editor plugin
Self-hosted desktop app - no cloud code exposure required
competitive_context.market_position: Turret positions itself as a higher-autonomy alternative to copilot-style assistants. While tools like Copilot and Cursor require constant developer interaction, Turret aims for true task delegation where developers describe goals and receive validated, merge-ready code. The desktop app approach provides full control over code privacy.

technical: Requires Claude Pro/Max subscription for API access
Depends on Claude Code CLI for agent execution
Python 3.12 specifically required (not 3.14) for native dependency compatibility
Electron app size can be large due to bundled runtime
Native dependencies (node-pty, real_ladybug) require C++ build tools on Windows
resources: Primary development by single core contributor (AndyMik90)
Small community of additional contributors (10+ contributors)
dependencies: Claude AI API (Anthropic) - core AI capability
Git for version control and worktree isolation
Linear for optional external task management integration
